title: Freeze and calibrate directional-pair definitions before scorer integration
statement: A new exploratory check uses the first 7,000 normalized words from each of three cleaned works (Augustine, Dante and Nibelungenlied), ten shuffles, one random monoalphabetic substitution and three independent equal-probability three-sign homophonic encodings. For each plaintext sample compare no removals, the single most frequent type, and the top ceil(1% of plaintext distinct types); use the same number of removals in each transformed sample. Ties are broken by first appearance. Count forward unequal-word pairs at distances 1–3, mark an unordered pair type skewed when absolute forward minus reverse counts exceed 5, and divide by the number of observed unordered pair types. Original skew ratios with no removals versus 1% removal are Latin 0.001982 to 0.000141, Italian 0.003644 to 0.000301, German 0.005210 to 0.000746. A bijective character substitution preserves the results exactly, and a planted five-symbol directional cycle is detected; in the tested toy homophonic encodings skew ratios are zero or near zero. In the no-removal samples, distinct types per token are 0.392, 0.307, 0.207, while hapax types per token are 0.289, 0.214, 0.107. These are different readings of unique words. Pair-type and pair-occurrence denominators also differ. This is a sensitivity pilot, not an exact replication or a manuscript result.
check: Resolve or explicitly choose the pair denominator, stopword percentage interpretation and unique-word measure, and preserve type/count semantics in a reviewed scorer primitive. Preregister sample length, window boundaries, stopword tie and cross-gap rules and evaluate on separate held-apart historical works; use multiple languages, independent witness transcriptions and planted positive and negative controls. Report both all pair types and occurrences, both distinct and singleton definitions, sensitivity to filtering, repeated seeded encodings and uncertainty. Freeze threshold and null calibration before any hidden-page evaluation.

methods.paper: https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3313/paper8.pdf, pages 3–5. Paper reports a 3-word forward/backward window, T=5, percentage frequency filtering and an ambiguous unique-word description; it does not justify treating this pilot as an exact implementation.
methods.sample: First 7,000 words of each P-J-011 cleaned training work. These source works have appeared in earlier calibration and are not independent confirmations. No manuscript words or hidden split read.
methods.pairing: After removal, concatenate retained tokens within each sample; count unequal ordered pairs forward at distances 1–3, group by unordered types. Count |forward-reverse| > 5 once per unordered type. The fixed 7,000-token windows and 1% grid were selected for this exploratory pilot, not used for any confirmatory threshold.
methods.controls: Distinct fixed-width 3-way random code for each character position, independent seeds 0–2; count removal k fixed to plaintext k even if encrypted vocabulary grows. Ten seeded word-order shuffles; monoalphabetic random permutation seed 408. Planted five-symbol cycle repeated 400 times; this is one easy positive control.
methods.limits: Samples are work beginnings, not randomized or independent works per language. Only one positive construction, three homophonic seeds, ten null permutations and a toy cipher. Stopword removal may create artificial adjacencies. No independent transcription comparison, review, full calibration or scorer primitive is complete.

reproduction.instruction: Extract experiments/P-J-011/mubadala777/step.json reproduction scripts to a temporary directory and run extract_works.py with PYTHONPATH set to the repository root. Put this script alongside clean_works.json, adjust its absolute path and run with Python 3.
